newsitem.title: Italy: Tremor hits north Italy, southern floods kill three.
newsitem.headline: Tremor hits north Italy, southern floods kill three.

text.p: An earthquake registering 4.8 on the Richter scale struck northern Italy on Tuesday, dislodging plaster and cornices from buildings near the epicentre and causing dozens of minor injuries.
An 86-year-old man died of a heart attack immediately after the tremor struck at 11:56 a.m. (0956 GMT), officials said.

The earthquake hit the north as heavy rain pounded the peninsula, causing scattered flooding from Venice in the north to the southern region of Calabria where three people were reported killed near the port of Crotone.
The National Geophysics Institute said the earthquake was centred in the northern region of Emilia Romagna.

It was felt as far south as Florence and in all areas of the north including Milan, Bolzano in the eastern Dolomites and Genoa on the western coast. The earthquake was also felt in Switzerland, the Swiss Seismological Service said.
"The earthquake was felt as far away as Zurich, especially in the upper levels of high-rise buildings," the service said.
Sensors around the Leaning Tower of Pisa also recorded the tremor, but experts who monitor the 12th century marble bell tower said it had not shifted any further.

Ten people in the town of Reggio Emilia, near the epicentre, were treated in hospital for minor injuries from falling plaster, while more than a dozen people in nearby Modena were treated for shock and minor injuries.
Other communities also reported that cornices had been shaken loose from buildings and churches, many located in historic districts.
Officials in the town of Correggio said an 86-year-old man, frightened by the tremor, died of a heart attack.

Authorities in towns around the epicentre said people ran into the streets in panic and electricity and telephone service was temporarily cut. Many people left work to check their homes for damage and schools were closed for safety checks.
State railways also suspended services between Bologna and Milan for about two hours to check the safety of bridges following the tremor.
The most serious flooding was in the southern industrial town of Crotone where three people, including a 72-year-old woman, were reported killed and another five were missing.

Heavy rains over two days caused the River Esaro to break its banks, flooding most roads in Crotone and disrupting rail service. Work in the industrial area had ground to a halt because water, electricity and telephone services were cut.
"The situation is very serious. Crotone is practically isolated," said Transport Ministry undersecretary Pino Soriero, who attended an emergency meeting in Crotone on Tuesday.
Venice's Saint Mark's Square and other areas of the lagoon city also were reported under water on Tuesday.
